published_source: Printed Table 4, column (2) ln(permits) of the published article (papers/mksc/mksc.2022.1409.pdf, Articles in Advance p. 7, main text; the table prints no N), read Nov 4 2026; differs from the code output -0.088483 (bootstrap SE 0.032001; authors' code on the deduplicated package data with did 2.5.1) by 0.0006, 0.7 percent: did package version (the authors used a 2022 GitHub build) and the duplicate 94606/94607 series in the authors' data (the as-shipped emulation gives -0.089036, 0.1 percent off). Earlier: Article Table 4 (Marketing Science 42(4), 2023; Articles in Advance p. 7): aggte(type='simple') of did::att_gt with bootstrap SE. Authors' code re-run on the deduplicated package data gives -0.088483 (bootstrap SE 0.032001, analytic 0.032802); on the shipped rows with the duplicate series emulated as separate units -0.089036.
replication_status: approximate (same sign, within 10 percent: printed -0.0891 (0.0327) vs code -0.0885 (0.0320), 0.7 percent; did package version difference and the deduplicated data, the as-shipped emulation -0.0890 is 0.1 percent off; verified against the article Nov 4 2026)
notes: Zipcode-month panel, months 72-215 (Jan 2008-Dec 2019), 755 zipcodes, unbalanced (cities enter the data at different months; two cities exit before Dec 2019). Treatment: binary, absorbing, from the unit-constant timing variable regulation_time (month the short-term-rental regulation took effect; 0 = never; 231 and 246 fall after the sample and are treated as never-treated, as did does). 13 in-sample cohorts (127,150,155,157,173,177,183,198,203,204,210,213,215; 638 zipcodes), 117 never-treated zipcodes (59 never regulated + 58 regulated after Dec 2019), no always-treated units, no switch-offs. Authors report Callaway-Sant'Anna only (did::att_gt, control_group='notyettreated', allow_unbalanced_panel=TRUE, no covariates, no weights, bootstrap SE clustered by zipcode); no TWFE regression exists in the package, the TWFE counterpart is D = 1[regulation_time > 0 & time >= regulation_time] with zipcode FE + month FE, clustered by zipcode. Outcomes are already ln(1+count) in the data file. DATA: the shipped repldid.csv (90,682 rows) has two rows per month for zipcodes 94606 and 94607 in months 72-138 (a second, 144-month series with zero permits), which did 2.5.1 rejects; data_path points to ~/did_packages/_work/mksc.2022.1409/repldid_dedup.csv (90,394 rows), the shipped rows that match the authors' own final-submission repldid.csv (identical file). Project member Davide Proserpio is a coauthor (PROTOCOL Section 6). Nov 2 audit: pipeline CSA now uses did's unbalanced-panel cells, as the authors do (pipeline_caveat updated; the composition-fixed values are kept as diag_ fields).
pipeline_caveat: Nov 2: the pipeline's Callaway-Sant'Anna step is did::att_gt(allow_unbalanced_panel = TRUE, control_group = 'notyettreated'), the same unbalanced-panel cells as the authors' code (PROTOCOL 5b revised Nov 2); the composition-fixed cells (units observed in both g-1 and t) are only a diagnostic column (csa_fc). Remaining differences from the published numbers: did 2.5.1 vs the authors' 2022 build, and the deduplicated data (see log).
csa_weights_note: Nov 2: the published CSA comes from R did (or staggered, whose estimates did reproduces), which weights cells by fixed cohort shares; Hull's DiD-averaging weights cells by treated-observation counts. 'did' reproduces the published number (main analysis, option B); the strict-Hull run (CSA_STRICT_HULL=1, option A) ignores this field.
